en: Jose Rizal built Dapitan's first water dam and improved local sanitation to successfully stop cholera outbreaks among the townspeople.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a low-cost bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm during hospital power outages.
Indigenous groups in the Philippines traditionally use lagundi leaves to safely and effectively treat coughs and respiratory infections.
The Filipino value of bayanihan helps neighbors quickly carry belongings and evacuate vulnerable families during dangerous typhoon floods.
The Executive branch's Department of Health mandates free childhood immunizations to prevent deadly diseases like measles and polio.
Decorators of the Pahiyas Festival use natural kiping leaves instead of plastics to prevent clogged drains and community flooding.
Exercising your civic duty to clean stagnant water around your house prevents mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever.
Barangay health workers learn local dialects to accurately explain medicine dosages, preventing accidental poisoning in young children.
Protecting the Philippine Eagle's forest habitat prevents severe soil erosion, which safeguards lowland communities from deadly landslides.
The 1991 Local Government Code empowers barangay captains to enforce curfews, protecting children from late-night accidents and crime.
The deep roots of the Narra, our national tree, stabilize soil on slopes to prevent dangerous landslides during heavy rains.
Eating traditional Filipino fermented foods like atchara provides healthy probiotics that improve digestion and boost the immune system.
